name: DUNCAN, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the state's failure to appoint counsel for an eligible defendant for an extended period violates the right to counsel under Article I, section 11 of the Oregon Constitution, and dismissal without prejudice is the required remedy after 60 or 90 days depending on the case type.

name: Flynn, C. J.
description: Other, did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: GARRETT, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the ballot title's caption, "yes" result statement, and summary must be modified to accurately reflect the measure's major effects, including the elimination of school district discretion and the non-speculative fiscal impact of funding following the student.

name: Ortega, P. J.
description: Concurred, argued that Measure 114 is a reasonable regulation to promote public safety and does not unduly frustrate the right to armed self-defense, thus being facially constitutional.

name: GARRETT, J.
description: Concurred, authored the main opinion, which affirmed the Court of Appeals' decision that the mandatory minimum sentence was not unconstitutionally disproportionate and that the trial court erred in considering the defendant's personal characteristics (mental health) in its proportionality analysis.

name: Balmer, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the majority's holding was more limited than the broad rule the defendant had proposed regarding personal characteristics in proportionality analysis.

name: Bushong, J.
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: DUNCAN, J.
description: Concurred, authored the majority opinion which reversed the Court of Appeals' decision on preservation grounds and remanded the case for further proceedings on the double jeopardy issue.

name: Bushong, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the majority's detailed discussion of the merits of the double jeopardy claim and related legal principles was dicta and should not influence the Court of Appeals on remand.

name: Baldwin, Senior Judge
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: JAMES, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the lack of a "right" to future employment does not, as a matter of law, prevent a plaintiff from proving economic damages for lost future wages, and that the trial court erred in dismissing the complaint.

name: BUSHONG, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the record did not demonstrate that the trial court's decision to deny the defendant's constitutional right to retained counsel of choice was a permissible exercise of its discretion, thus requiring reversal and remand for a new trial.

name: GARRETT, J.
description: Concurred, argued that Governor Kotek lacked authority to revoke the conditional commutation because plaintiff had already completed her sentence, and the terms of the commutation and acceptance agreement did not grant such authority after sentence expiration.

name: GARRETT, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Governor's commutation rendered the petitioner's request for resentencing moot because he was no longer serving a death sentence, and that his challenges to penalty-phase questions were procedurally barred due to lack of preservation.

name: Walters, Senior Judge, Justice pro tempore
Masih, J.
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: JAMES, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Court of Appeals erred by analyzing the seizure under a criminal framework instead of an administrative one, and remanded for reconsideration.

name: DUNCAN, J.
description: Concurred, arguing that the totality of circumstances, including the defendant's probation status and the coercive environment, made the interrogation compelling, requiring Miranda warnings.

name: Balmer, S. J.
description: Concurred, arguing that the state's conduct, including offering concrete benefits and implicitly guiding Layman's investigation, objectively conveyed that Layman was authorized to continue questioning defendant and could expect a reward, thus rendering him a state agent after the second proffer meeting.

name: Nelson, J.
description: Did not participate in the decision of this case due to resignation.

name: James, J.
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: GARRETT, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the UTPA provisions ORS 646.608(1)(b) and (1)(e) do not implicitly require proof that misrepresentations were "material to consumer purchasing decisions" and are not facially unconstitutional under free speech provisions.

name: Balmer, Senior Judge, Justice pro tempore
Walters, Senior Judge, Justice pro tempore
Nelson, J.
description: Did not participate in the decision of this case.

name: Bushong, J.
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: James, J.
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: DUNCAN, J.
description: Concurred, argued that detectives violated the defendant's right to counsel under Article I, section 11, of the Oregon Constitution by questioning him about charged FIP crimes without notifying his counsel, requiring suppression of the resulting evidence.

name: NELSON, J.
description: Concurred, argued that ORS 138.105(5) precludes appellate review of legal challenges to a conviction based on a guilty or no contest plea, interpreting "conviction" as the judicial determination of guilt reflected in the judgment.

name: Nakamoto, J.
description: Other, did not participate in the decision of this case.

name: NELSON, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the defendant failed to establish a causal connection between the state's delays and the prejudice from the lost booking video, thus no speedy trial violation occurred.

name: Balmer, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the five-day retention of the defendant's phone without a warrant was unlawful, but the error in admitting derivative evidence was harmless, thus affirming the conviction.

name: Baldwin, Senior Judge, Justice pro tempore
DeHoog, J.
description: Other, did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: GARRETT, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Oregon Constitution's Article I, section 11, grants a defendant the right to have counsel present in the grand jury room for consultation during testimony, but not for direct examination or formal evidentiary objections.

name: BALMER, J.
description: Concurred, argued that voters with inactive registration are not "qualified voters" because they are not eligible to vote, and therefore their signatures on initiative petitions should not be counted.

name: DUNCAN, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the "per se exigency rule" of the automobile exception was not well-founded, created confusion, was inconsistent with recent cases, and was no longer justified by technological and legislative changes, thus requiring actual exigent circumstances for warrantless vehicle searches.

name: Landau, Senior Judge, Justice pro tempore
Balmer, J.
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: KISTLER, S.J.
description: Concurred, argued that a defective waiver of a preliminary hearing does not deprive a circuit court of subject matter jurisdiction, reversing the Court of Appeals decision.

name: Balmer, J.
description: Other, did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: WALTERS, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the court has authority to modify constitutional deadlines to ensure reapportionment occurs based on federal census data and in time for the election cycle, given the unforeseen delay in census data release.

name: WALTERS, C.J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion, arguing that the trial court's order compelling the defendant to unlock her cell phone violated her right against self-incrimination because the state failed to meet the required burden of proof and did not prohibit the use of the compelled act against the defendant.
